app.title: BVID-FE — Barely Visible Impact Damage analysis
app.summary: A person describes a damaged laminate panel in a sidebar: material, ply stack, panel size, and the damage source. The damage can be an impact event to predict from, or a measured inspection file to load. Before running, a live preview estimates the energy at which damage starts and the predicted damage area. The person picks a model tier and loading mode, runs the analysis, and reads the pristine strength, the residual strength and the knockdown, with views of the damage footprint, a 3D damaged mesh, a through-thickness severity heatmap and buckling modes. The person can sweep impact energy to get a knockdown curve as a CSV. Finally they fill in a nonconformance report that attaches the analysis and a proposed disposition with flags and criteria, and export it as Markdown and JSON.

task.text: Predict how much strength an impact-damaged laminate keeps and turn that into a nonconformance report with a proposed disposition for a review board.

data.text: A configuration of one laminate panel and its damage, given as an impact event or as measured delamination ellipses from an inspection JSON. Results are strengths, a damage state over the panel, an energy sweep table and a report form.
data.item: one impacted composite panel with its ply stack and damage state

stage.text: assessing an impact-damaged part after inspection, before a review board decides its disposition

mechanism.text: Sidebar inputs build one analysis configuration, which is synced to a shareable URL and can be filled from presets. A run fills a row of result tabs: summary numbers, a damage map, a 3D mesh, a severity heatmap, a buckling chart and an energy sweep. The last tab turns the latest result and a form into a nonconformance report with a rule-based disposition recommendation.

field.text: residual-strength prediction for impact-damaged composite laminates in aerospace damage tolerance

workflow.name: estimate a damaged specimen's remaining capacity and file a disposition report

steps.here: material, ply angles and panel size in the sidebar, with an optional preset. The damage source is either an impact event (energy, impactor) or an uploaded inspection JSON of delamination ellipses, and the run button is blocked until that file loads.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: a live preview of the onset energy and the predicted damage area, then Run analysis on the chosen tier (empirical, semi_analytical, fe3d) gives pristine strength, residual strength and knockdown
tabs show the delamination footprint map, a 3D damaged mesh, a through-thickness severity heatmap and buckling mode values

steps.step: compare across a range of conditions
steps.here: an energy sweep over a list of energies on a chosen tier draws a knockdown-vs-energy curve, lists any failed points, and downloads as CSV
a nonconformance form (part, station, type, description, dent threshold) gets a proposed disposition banded from the knockdown, dent and fiber breakage, with flags and criteria in a previewed report
the report downloads as Markdown and JSON, and the results as JSON

distinctive: three model tiers of rising cost, from milliseconds to a 3D finite-element solve, are chosen per run, and an oversized mesh is refused before it is solved
damage comes either from a predicted impact event or from measured inspection ellipses, so prediction and as-found assessment share one path
the disposition recommendation is banded by strength retention, a dent detectability threshold and fiber breakage, and is always marked as proposed until a review board approves it
the configuration is written to the URL and stale results are flagged when inputs change after a run
